Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Regional GRA Customs intercepts suspected smuggled goods worth GH¢1.8m at Tatale Source : Adomonline 18 November 2026 2:47pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has intercepted suspected smuggled goods worth more than GH¢1.8 million at Tatale in the Northern Region. The goods were stored in a heavily secured warehouse.
The seizure followed an intelligence-led operation against suspected smuggling in the area. The items included thousands of bags of rice and sugar, along with a quantity of cooking oil.
The find is part of the Customs Division’s push against smuggling and other activities that cut into revenue and weaken the enforcement of Ghana’s trade laws.
The interception is also expected to help stop the illegal movement of goods across the country’s borders and protect legitimate businesses from unfair competition.
The GRA has not said who owns the warehouse, where the products came from, or whether anyone has been arrested.
